title: Relations are emitted (and scored "asociacion_fuerte"/"Alta") on evidence text that does not contain one of the two entities
whatIsWrong: _overlap_context() returns a.sentence only when the two mentions share a sentence; otherwise it returns whichever single mention's context window is longer. That window is built with context_radius (default 260) around one mention, while the pair filter allows a start-to-start distance up to 699 chars. Whenever distance > ~radius the returned 'shared evidence' is a one-sided window that provably does not contain the other entity. All cue matching for the relation (association, strong_association, speculative, negation -> the +4/+4/-2/-4 bonuses and the association label) is then run on that one-sided text, and the string is exported as evidence_text — the module docstring promises 'every row carries the evidence string the reviewer can re-read'.
concreteFailure: Article text: 'Methods We measured cadmium exposure in urine samples of the cohort.' + 520 chars of unrelated filler about water sampling + 'Renal outcomes including nephropathy were significantly associated with the biomarker.' Executed end-to-end (extract_mentions with context_radius=260, then build_relations with relation_distance=900): cadmium@20 (methods), nephropathy@615 (methods), distance=595, different sentences. Output: 1 relation, association=asociacion_fuerte, confidence=Alta, confidence_score=26, evidence_text = the nephropathy window only. Assertion 'cadmium' in evidence.lower() -> False. The pipeline therefore reports a high-confidence, strongly-associated cadmium-nephropathy pair whose quoted evidence never mentions cadmium, and whose 'significantly associated' cue belongs to a sentence about a different variable.
suggestedFix: Build the evidence span from the text actually spanning both mentions, e.g. article.text[min(a.start,b.start)-pad : max(a.end,b.end)+pad], and require that both matched_text strings occur in it before emitting the relation; run the cue matching on that joint span only. Cross-sentence pairs whose joint span exceeds a documented maximum should be dropped or flagged as 'cooccurrence_only'.

verdict.refutationOrConfirmation: CONFIRMED, and worse in production than the report claims. I reproduced the synthetic case independently (cadmium@20 methods, nephropathy@614, distance 594, different sentences, relation_distance=900): 1 relation, association=asociacion_fuerte, confidence=Alta, score=26, evidence_text = the nephropathy window only, 'cadmium' not present. I then re-scored the shipped corpus in /Users/drux/Documents/Drux/1_UNAM_FESI/RevisionContaminantes/outputs/review_miner/relations.csv (936 rows) by matching each row's entity ids back to their lexicon regexes: only 451/936 rows have BOTH entities inside evidence_text; 322 rows are missing entity A, 163 missing entity B, and 232 of the entity-missing rows still carry an association label (asociacion_fuerte/debil). Sampled rows include 'metales pesados / neurodegeneracion general, asociacion_fuerte, Alta, 28' whose evidence is a journal affiliation block, and 'cadmio / Esclerosis lateral amiotrofica, asociacion_fuerte, Alta, 30' whose evidence is a reference-list entry. Not deliberate design: the module docstring at relations.py:3-7 states the pair must 'share enough local context ... to ground the association in a single quotable fragment' and that 'every row carries the evidence string the reviewer can re-read'. Nothing downstream re-checks that both entities appear in the evidence. Severity critical is correct: it is the single claim the exported relation table makes.

title: Hardcoded 700 in _overlap_context silently caps the protocol's configurable relation_distance at 699
whatIsWrong: build_relations() accepts relation_distance (fed from protocol.analysis.relation_distance, default 900, wizard slider range 100-3000 per src/lib/protocol/defaults.ts ANALYSIS_BOUNDS). The candidate filter uses that value, but _overlap_context then returns "" for any cross-sentence pair with |a.start-b.start| >= 700, and the caller drops empty evidence. Any relation_distance above 700 is therefore inert: the analysis parameter the user tunes and reports in the methods section does not do what it says.
concreteFailure: Sweep over d = 0..1599 with cross-sentence mentions, executed: relation_distance=400 keeps d in [0,400]; relation_distance=700, 900, 1500 and 3000 all keep exactly d in [0,699]. Direct proof: a pair at d=800 with relation_distance=900 passes the distance filter (abs(800) > 900 is False) but _overlap_context returns '' and 0 relations are built; the same pair at d=699 yields 1 relation. A protocol documenting 'relation window = 900 characters' actually mines a 699-character window.

relations.py:64  relation_distance: int = 900,
relations.py:78  if abs(a.start - b.start) > relation_distance and a.sentence != b.sentence: continue
Executed (t2.py): relation_distance=  900 -> pairs kept for |a.start-b.start| in [0, 699]; relation_distance= 3000 -> pairs kept for |a.start-b.start| in [0, 699]
suggestedFix: Pass relation_distance into _overlap_context and compare against it instead of the literal 700 (or delete the second test entirely, since the caller already enforces the distance bound).

verdict.refutationOrConfirmation: CONFIRMED by independent sweep. Built cross-sentence mention pairs at every distance 0..1599 and ran build_relations for relation_distance in {400,700,900,1500,3000}: 400 keeps d in [0,400] (401 values, so the parameter works below the cap), while 700, 900, 1500 and 3000 all keep exactly d in [0,699] (700 values). The hardcoded 700 in _overlap_context (relations.py:28) therefore makes any configured relation_distance above 700 inert, and the wizard exposes the slider up to 3000 (src/lib/protocol/defaults.ts:197 ANALYSIS_BOUNDS.relationDistance = {min:100,max:3000}), while ProtocolRunner.tsx:312 prints the configured value into the methods narrative. One nuance the report does not state but that does not rescue it: same-sentence pairs bypass the distance filter entirely (relations.py:78 requires a.sentence != b.sentence), so the 699 cap binds only on cross-sentence pairs — which is precisely the population relation_distance exists to control. title: INFORMATIVE_SECTIONS omits 'introduction', so role_intro_discussion_only can never be assigned to introduction-only entities — they become role_unclear
whatIsWrong: INFORMATIVE_SECTIONS = {title, abstract, methods, results, discussion, conclusion} excludes 'introduction' and 'other'. _assign_role reaches the ROLE_INTRO_DISCUSSION branch only when informative_count > 0, and since CENTRAL_SECTIONS is a subset of INFORMATIVE_SECTIONS, that branch is in practice fed by title/abstract/methods/results/discussion/conclusion mentions. Consequence in both directions: (a) an entity mentioned exclusively in the Introduction — the textbook case the role is named for — falls through to ROLE_UNCLEAR; (b) an entity mentioned only in Results or Methods with a sub-threshold score is labelled 'intro/discussion only'. Both mislabellings propagate to visual_analytics.ROLE_WEIGHT (role_intro_discussion_only=0.5, role_unclear=0.5) and to the reported role distribution.
concreteFailure: Executed _assign_role with default weights: 3 mentions only in 'introduction', no cues -> role_unclear (score 3). 8 mentions only in 'introduction' each with an exposure cue -> role_unclear, score=40 — an entity discussed at length in the Introduction is reported as 'unclear' rather than 'intro/discussion only'. Conversely, 1 mention in 'results' with no cues -> role_intro_discussion_only (score 5), and 1 mention in 'title' -> role_intro_discussion_only. Brute force over all <=3-mention configurations confirms no configuration containing only introduction mentions ever yields role_intro_discussion_only.

suggestedFix: Add 'introduction' to INFORMATIVE_SECTIONS, and gate the ROLE_INTRO_DISCUSSION branch on non-central informative sections (introduction/discussion/conclusion) so that a central-section-only entity with a low score falls to ROLE_UNCLEAR or a dedicated low-evidence role instead.

title: Cue bonuses are section-independent, so bibliography mentions carry a net-positive score and can promote an entity to role_primary_focus
whatIsWrong: mention_score() adds the cue bonuses (+4 exposure, +5 dose, +2 association) on top of section_weight without any section-dependent damping. The 'references' weight is -3, smaller in magnitude than a single dose (+5) or exposure (+4) cue, so a mention inside the reference list scores +2 (dose), +1 (exposure) or up to +8 (all three). Cue detection runs on a 260-char context window, and reference lists are dense with cited titles containing 'dose', 'exposure', 'associated'. The ROLE_BIBLIOGRAPHIC guard only fires when EVERY mention is in references (sections_count['references'] == n_mentions), so a single central mention lets an arbitrarily large pile of bibliographic hits drive the score past the >=16 primary-focus threshold.
concreteFailure: Executed with default weights: an entity with 1 title mention (no cues) and 6 references mentions whose context matches the dose family scores 5 + 6*(-3+5) = 17 >= 16, central_count=1, direct_cues=6 -> role_primary_focus, confidence_score=17. The same entity with the identical 6 reference mentions but no cue matches scores -13 -> role_intro_discussion_only. In other words, the top role ('primary focus of the study', ROLE_WEIGHT 3.0 in visual_analytics) is reachable from a single title hit plus bibliography noise. Per-section max scores measured: references min=-7, base=-3, max=+8.

classify.py:192-195  bibliographic guard requires sections_count["references"] == n_mentions; primary focus needs central_count>0 and score>=16 and direct_cues>0
Executed (t1.py): '1 title + 6 references w/ dose cue -> role_primary_focus score=17'; '1 title + 6 references NO cue -> role_intro_discussion_only score=-13'; per-section table 'references w=-3 min=-7 base=-3 max=8'
suggestedFix: Clamp each mention's contribution so that a negatively-weighted section cannot become positive (e.g. score = max(0, section_weight + bonuses) when section_weight < 0), or exclude 'references' mentions from the aggregate score and from direct_cues entirely, keeping them only for the bibliographic-only test.

verdict.refutationOrConfirmation: CONFIRMED synthetically AND on the real corpus. Synthetic: 1 title mention + 6 references mentions with a dose cue -> role_primary_focus, score 17; the same shape with no cues -> role_intro_discussion_only, score -13; 6 references-only mentions with dose cues -> role_bibliographic_only (guard fires only when every mention is in references, as claimed). The top role in the systematic-review table is demonstrably reachable from bibliography noise on this author's own data. High is correct.

title: Relation section is always the A-side mention's section (tautological expression), making association strength asymmetric between the two variable slots
whatIsWrong: `section = a.section if a.section == b.section else a.section` evaluates to a.section in every case — the conditional is a no-op left over from the refactor. That section is then used by _association_label (asociacion_fuerte requires section in CENTRAL_SECTIONS) and by _relation_confidence (Alta requires section in CENTRAL_SECTIONS), and is exported as the relation's section. For cross-section pairs the label therefore depends on which slot the protocol author happened to assign to Variable A, even though the module docstring states A and B are interchangeable slots whose meaning lives only in the display labels.
concreteFailure: Executed with identical evidence text ('cadmium showed an odds ratio of 2.1 for nephropathy'), identical cues and identical confidence_score=19: with A in 'results' and B in 'discussion' the relation is section=results, association=asociacion_fuerte, confidence=Alta; with A in 'discussion' and B in 'results' the same pair becomes section=discussion, association=asociacion_debil, confidence=Media. Swapping which variable is slot A changes the reported strength of the association for the same textual evidence. The exported section can also contradict the evidence text, which may come from the B-side context window (see _overlap_context).
evidence:
relations.py:83  section = a.section if a.section == b.section else a.section
Executed (t4.py): 'A=results,B=discussion   -> section=results    assoc=asociacion_fuerte conf=Alta  score=19' / 'A=discussion,B=results   -> section=results is not chosen: section=discussion assoc=asociacion_debil conf=Media score=19'
suggestedFix: Make the choice explicit and slot-symmetric: use the section of the mention the evidence text was taken from, or take the more central of the two sections (e.g. prefer a section in CENTRAL_SECTIONS), and record both sections in the exported row.

verdict.refutationOrConfirmation: CONFIRMED. relations.py:83 reads `section = a.section if a.section == b.section else a.section`, which is textually a no-op (verified by string match against the live file). I built two relations with identical evidence text ('cadmium showed an odds ratio of 2.1 for nephropathy'), identical cues and identical confidence_score=15, differing only in which slot held which section: A=results/B=discussion -> section=results, asociacion_fuerte, Alta; A=discussion/B=results -> section=discussion, asociacion_debil, Media. Swapping the slots flips the reported strength of the association for byte-identical evidence, because _association_label (relations.py:49) and _relation_confidence (relations.py:34) both gate on CENTRAL_SECTIONS membership of that one section value. This is not defensible as design — the module docstring (relations.py:9-12) states the A/B slots are interchangeable and their meaning lives only in display labels. Medium is the right level: it only bites on cross-section pairs (both mentions within 699 chars but straddling a detected header boundary), which is a minority of pairs, and the dead conditional shows an intended third branch was lost in a refactor.

title: detect_sections is non-deterministic: sorted(set(markers)) makes the section label at a tied offset depend on PYTHONHASHSEED
whatIsWrong: markers always starts with (0,'title'). When a section header regex also matches at offset 0 -- which happens whenever the extracted PDF text begins with a header line such as 'Abstract' -- markers contains (0,'title') and (0,'abstract'). `sorted(set(markers), key=lambda item: item[0])` sorts only on the offset; Python's sort is stable, so the winner is whichever tuple the SET iterates first. Set iteration order for tuples containing strings depends on string hashing, which is randomized per process by default. The loser is then silently deleted by the `if end > start` filter (its span has length 0). Result: the same file, same protocol, same code produces a different section label -- and therefore a different section weight -- on different runs. Weight('title')=5 vs weight('abstract')=4 feeds classify.mention_score, summarize_entity's confidence_score, relation scores and _relation_confidence thresholds, so downstream classifications can flip between runs. A published pipeline must be bit-reproducible.

title: clean_pdf_text de-hyphenation is unconditional and can span blank lines, destroying required hyphens and gluing two mentions into one unmatchable token
whatIsWrong: `re.sub(r"(\\w)-\\s*\\n\\s*(\\w)", r"\\1\\2", text)` joins every hyphen that precedes a newline, with no test for whether the hyphen is a soft line-break hyphen or a lexically required one. Genuinely hyphenated study-design and compound terms are silently corrupted. Worse, `\\s*` matches across a blank line, so a paragraph that happens to end in a hyphen is glued to the first word of the next paragraph, producing a token in which neither original word is `\\b`-matchable -- both mentions are lost, and the lexicon has no way to recover them.
concreteFailure: Executed: 'We conducted a population-based case-\\ncontrol study of self-\\nreported lead exposure.\\nDose-\\nresponse was linear.' -> 'population-based casecontrol study of selfreported lead exposure.\\nDoseresponse was linear.' After cleaning, none of 'case-control', 'case control', 'dose-response', 'self-reported' is present; classify.detect_article_kind's hardcoded epidem_markers tuple (which contains literally 'case-control' and 'case control', classify.py:78-79) can no longer fire on that text. Second case: '...blood lead-\\n\\nDementia risk was higher.' -> '...blood leadDementia risk was higher.'; re.search(r'\\blead\\b') is False and re.search(r'\\bdementia\\b') is False -- one Variable-A mention and one Variable-B mention are both destroyed, and with them any relation between them.

  'case-control' present after cleaning: False
  'dose-response' present after cleaning: False
  OUT : '...blood leadDementia risk was higher.'
    \blead\b matches: False
    \bdementia\b matches: False

title: _weight_relation multiplies two non-independent quantities: confidence is derived from association, so the declared 3:2:1 association weighting is realized as 9:3.89:1
whatIsWrong: `weighted_score = ASSOCIATION_WEIGHT[association] * CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT[confidence]` treats association level and confidence as two independent evidence dimensions. They are not: relations._relation_confidence() computes confidence FROM the association label. `mencion_especulativa` can never be anything but 'Baja' (Alta requires association=='asociacion_fuerte', Media requires association in {fuerte, debil}), so its weight is structurally pinned at exactly 1.0 and CONFIDENCE_WEIGHT can never modulate it. And because _association_label only emits 'asociacion_fuerte' inside CENTRAL_SECTIONS, the score for a strong relation is essentially always >= 12, so fuerte is essentially always 'Alta'. The product therefore squares the association signal instead of combining two sources of evidence. This weight drives bubble radii (line 390), bipartite edge widths (line 471), the top-pairs bar chart, both heatmaps, and three k-means feature families — i.e. every quantitative claim in the figure set. Compounding it, the same scalar `weight` is added to relation_association::, relation_confidence:: AND relation_section:: (lines 175-177), so the relation block carries 3x the mass of any entity block in the standardized Euclidean k-means distance.
concreteFailure: On the shipped 936-relation corpus: asociacion_fuerte -> Alta in 149/149 cases (100%), mencion_especulativa -> Baja in 106/106 (100%, structurally forced), asociacion_debil -> Media in 313/331 (94.6%). Mean realized weight per association = 9.000 (fuerte), 3.891 (debil), 1.000 (especulativa) = ratio 9.00 : 3.89 : 1.00, versus the declared ASSOCIATION_WEIGHT ratio 3 : 2 : 1. A strong association is therefore rendered 2.31x larger in the bubble/edge/bar figures than the protocol's own weight table says it should be relative to a weak one (9/3.89 = 2.31 vs the intended 1.50).

title: Run-status polling stops permanently after a single failed poll, freezing the UI at 'running'; jobs also live only in an unbounded in-memory Map
whatIsWrong: The polling effect reschedules only through setJob(next); on `!response.ok` it returns and on a thrown fetch it swallows the error, in both cases without arming a new timer. Since the effect's dependency array is [job] and job did not change, no further poll is ever scheduled — contradicting the code's own comment 'network blip — try again on next interval'. This is reachable in normal use because jobs.ts stores jobs only in a process-global Map (globalThis.__nexoJobs) with no persistence and no eviction: a dev-server restart or a Next dev recompile of the route makes GET /api/pipeline/status?jobId=... return 404, which is exactly the !response.ok branch. The same Map never evicts finished jobs, so every run (with up to 500 log lines) is retained for the life of the process.
concreteFailure: Start a run; the server process restarts (or one poll 404s/500s/times out). The Python pipeline keeps running and writes its outputs, but the UI stays on 'En proceso' forever with no error and no results link, and there is no way to recover the job id — GET /api/pipeline/status returns {"error":"No se encontro la ejecucion solicitada."} 404 for that id permanently.

pipeline/status/route.ts:12-15 returns 404 when the id is absent.

title: A missing or headers-less sections.json silently collapses the whole corpus into section "title" (weight 5), inflating every score and making role_bibliographic_only unreachable

The reference-list penalty (-3) becomes +5, an 8-point swing per bibliographic mention; `central_count` becomes equal to `n_mentions` for every entity, so the `sections_count['references'] == n_mentions` guard in classify.py:_assign_role can never fire and `role_bibliographic_only` becomes unreachable. Nothing is logged, no warning is emitted, and the run completes and exports normally. The same silent path is taken by a hand-written or older sections.json that has `weights` but no `headers` block, because `headers_raw` then falls back to `{}` and every family compiles to an empty pattern list.
concreteFailure: Executed on the same 2-article corpus with the same protocol, once with sections.json and once with it deleted. title: Every baseline frequency/heat figure silently drops all entities beyond the 35th and truncates labels at 52 characters, with no note in the figure or its caption
whatIsWrong: `_svg_bar()` starts with `items = [(label, value) for label, value in items if value > 0][:35]`. All five baseline figures (frecuencia_<A>.svg, frecuencia_<B>.svg, tipo_estudio.svg, nivel_asociacion.svg and, through the same helper, the section/category bar charts) therefore render at most 35 bars. Because the callers pass `Counter.most_common()`, the dropped entities are always the least frequent ones — the long tail that a systematic review specifically needs to report. No annotation, ellipsis, "n de N mostrados" label or caption text records the truncation, and `fileDescription()`/FIGURE_DESCRIPTIONS in the Word report and results UI describe these figures as the frequency of detected entities without qualification. Bar labels are additionally silently cut at 52 characters (`label[:52]`), which can render two distinct long entity names identically.
concreteFailure: The project's own shipped Variable-A lexicon (config/review_miner_contaminants.json) declares 39 entities. Feeding 39 distinct entities into `_svg_bar` produces an SVG containing exactly 35 bars; entities ranked 36-39 are absent from the file with no trace. A reader of the published figure "Frecuencia de contaminantes detectados" would conclude those four contaminants were never detected in the corpus.

    items = [(label, value) for label, value in items if value > 0][:35]
review_miner/visualize.py:57
    ... >{html.escape(label[:52])}</text>

suggestedFix: Either render all entities (the SVG height is already computed from `len(items)`), or keep the cap and stamp the truncation into the figure itself and into FIGURE_DESCRIPTIONS/DESCRIPTIONS — e.g. "mostrando 35 de 39 entidades detectadas" — so no published figure under-reports without saying so. Do the same for the 52-character label clipping.
